title: Zanzibari-Inspired Golden Lamb Hand Pies
subtitle: plus Mixed Greens Salad with Cucumber, Almonds & Mango Dressing

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to middle position (middle and top positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 425 degrees. Wash and dry produce. Sprinkle half the flour over a clean work surface. Remove dough from packaging; place on floured surface. Halve dough (you’ll have two pieces; four pieces for 4). Roll each piece in flour to lightly coat, shaking any excess back onto work surface. TIP: Spray your hands with nonstick cooking spray or dust with flour to prevent sticking. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel; let rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: While dough rests, trim and halve cucumber lengthwise; thinly slice crosswise into half-moons. Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add lamb*, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until browned and cooked through, 3-5 minutes. TIP: If there’s excess grease in your pan, carefully pour it out. Add tomato paste; cook until fragrant and brick red in color, about 30 seconds. Add Tunisian Spice Blend, ½ cup water, and 2 tsp sugar (1 cup water and 4 tsp sugar for 4 servings); cook until thickened and water has almost evaporated, 30-60 seconds more. Remove from heat and let cool.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Once dough has rested 15 minutes, sprinkle remaining flour over work surface. Using a rolling pin, roll each piece of dough into a rough 5-inch circle (you’ll be shaping the dough again later, so no need to be perfect!). Cover with a clean kitchen towel and let rest 10 minutes more. Meanwhile, place 2 TBSP butter (4 TBSP for 4 servings) in a small microwave-safe bowl; microwave until melted, 15-30 seconds. Stir in ¼ tsp turmeric (½ tsp for 4). (Be sure to measure the turmeric—we sent more!)

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Once dough has rested 10 minutes, stretch each dough circle into a larger circle, about 8 inches wide; place on a parchment-lined baking sheet (two baking sheets for 4 servings). Place lamb filling on bottom half of each dough circle, leaving a ½-inch border. Lightly brush edges with water using a pastry brush or your fingers. Fold dough over filling and gently press edges together. Using a fork, press along edges to seal.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Brush hand pies all over with turmeric butter; using a sharp knife, gently cut two small, shallow diagonal slits along the top of each hand pie. Bake on middle rack until golden brown and crisp, 15-18 minutes (for 4 servings, bake on middle and top racks, swapping rack positions halfway through). Let cool for 5 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: While hand pies cool, in a second small bowl, whisk together chutney, vinegar, and a large drizzle of olive oil. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. In a large bowl, toss together mixed greens and cucumber. Drizzle with as much mango dressing as you like; toss to coat. Divide hand pies and salad between plates. Garnish salad with almonds. Serve.

title: Roasted Steak & Pineapple-Soy Glazed Broccoli

instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to middle position (middle and top positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 425 degrees. appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

title: Savory Mushroom & Spinach Ramen
subtitle: with Hoisin Miso Broth, Chili Crisp & Crispy Onions

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Wash and dry produce. Trim and quarter mushrooms (skip if your mushrooms are pre-sliced!). Once water is boiling, add noodles to pot. Cook, stirring, until just tender, 1-2 minutes. Drain and rinse noodles under cold water for at least 30 seconds, then toss with a drizzle of oil. Keep empty pot handy for next step.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In pot used for noodles, combine hoisin, miso sauce concentrates, pho stock concentrates, and 3 cups water (6 cups for 4 servings). Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer until ready to serve. TIP: Taste broth and season with salt if desired.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: While broth simmers, heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and softened, 6-8 minutes. Stir in spinach and cook, stirring constantly, until wilted, 30-60 seconds. Add half the soy sauce (all for 4 servings); stir to coat.

instructions_json.title: Divide noodles between large soup bowls
instructions_json.body: Divide noodles between large soup bowls. Pour broth over noodles. Top with mushrooms and spinach and any remaining sauce from pan. Top with as much chili crisp as you like. Garnish with crispy fried onions and serve. TIP: Add the onions as you eat to keep them nice and crispy.

version_notes: Official HelloFresh v1 Recipe (Normalized to 4 Servings)

title: Moo Shu Shrimp Lettuce Wraps
subtitle: with Red Cabbage & Sriracha-Lime Mayo

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry produce.Quarter lime. Trim and discard root end from lettuce; separate leaves; thinly slice 1-2 small center leaves.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, juice from one lime wedge (two wedges for 4 servings), salt, pepper, and as much Sriracha as you like. Add water 1 tsp at a time until mixture reaches a drizzling consistency.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add pork* and cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes.Stir in cabbage; cook, stirring occasionally, until just tender, 2-3 minutes.Add hoisin, chili sauce, and 2½ TBSP sweet soy glaze (5 TBSP for 4 servings) (be sure to measure the sweet soy glaze—we sent more!). Stir until thoroughly combined.Turn off heat. Stir in juice from two lime wedges (four wedges for 4). Taste and season with salt and pepper.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Divide lettuce leaves between plates; fill with shredded lettuce and moo shu pork. Drizzle with Sriracha-lime mayo and serve with any remaining lime wedges on the side.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

title: Sweet & Savory Chicken Bowls
subtitle: with Broccoli, Pickled Cucumber & Sesame Scallion Rice

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry produce. Trim and thinly slice cucumber. Thinly slice scallions, separating whites from greens. Cut broccoli into bite-size pieces if necessary. In a small bowl, combine cucumber, vinegar, ½ tsp sugar (1 tsp for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Set aside to pickle until ready to serve.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a small pot (medium pot for 4 servings) over medium-high heat. Add scallion whites and cook, stirring, until softened, 1-2 minutes.Stir in rice, 1¼ cups water (2¼ cups for 4), half the sesame oil (all for 4), and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to a low simmer. Cook until rice is tender, 15-18 minutes.Keep covered off heat until ready to serve.

appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: While rice cooks, pat chicken dry with paper towels; season all over with salt and pepper. In a medium bowl, combine chicken, half the cornstarch, and a big pinch of salt. Stir until chicken is fully coated. Heat a large drizzle of oil in a large, preferably nonstick, pan over medium-high heat. Add coated chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, 5-7 minutes. (TIP: Depending on the size of your pan, you may need to work in batches.) Reserve bowl. Turn off heat; transfer to a plate. Wipe out pan and let cool slightly.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in pan used for tofu over medium-high heat. Add broccoli and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, 6-8 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: While broccoli cooks, in bowl used for chicken, whisk together hoisin, sweet soy glaze, Sriracha, remaining cornstarch, and ⅓ cup water (⅔ cup for 4 servings). Reduce heat under pan with broccoli to low and stir in hoisin-soy mixture. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce is thickened and sticky, 1-2 minutes. Transfer seared chicken to pan. Stir until fully coated and chicken is warmed through, 1 minute. Taste and season with salt and pepper if desired.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Divide rice between bowls; top with chicken and broccoli and pickled cucumber (draining first) in separate sections. Garnish with scallion greens and serve.

title: Soy-Marinated Lamb Chops & Sesame Fried Rice
subtitle: with Edamame, Chili-Lemon Butter & Quick-Pickled Cucumber

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Place 2 TBSP butter (4 TBSP for 4 servings) in a small microwave-safe bowl; bring to room temperature. Wash and dry produce. Peel and mince garlic. Zest and quarter lemon.Pat steak* dry with paper towels. Place in a medium bowl with half the garlic, half the fish sauce, half the soy sauce, a drizzle of oil, and a squeeze of lemon juice (big squeeze for 4). Stir to fully coat steak. Set aside to marinate until ready to use in Step 4.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a small pot, combine rice, 1¼ cups water (2¼ cups for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to a low simmer. Cook until rice is tender, 15-18 minutes.Keep rice covered off heat until ready to use in Step 5.While rice cooks, trim and thinly slice cucumber into rounds. Trim and thinly slice scallions, separating whites from greens.

appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: In a second medium bowl, combine cucumber, scallion greens, vinegar, ½ tsp sugar, and ½ tsp salt (1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt for 4 servings). Set aside to pickle until ready to serve.To bowl with softened butter, add lemon zest, remaining fish sauce, and chili flakes to taste. Stir to combine; form into two equal portions (four portions for 4). TIP: If butter is not yet softened, microwave for 10 seconds.Refrigerate until firm and ready to serve.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Remove steak from marinade, allowing excess to drip off. Discard remaining marinade. Add steak to pan; cook to desired doneness, 3-6 minutes per side.Turn off heat; transfer steak to a cutting board and tent with foil to keep warm. Wipe out pan.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Once rice is done, heat a large drizzle of oil in pan used for steak over medium-high heat. Add edamame, scallion whites, half the sesame seeds, and remaining garlic. Cook until browned and fragrant, 1-2 minutes.Stir in rice, gently breaking up any clumps with the back of a wooden spoon; cook, undisturbed, until rice begins to crisp, 2-3 minutes.Stir in remaining soy sauce; continue to cook, stirring constantly, until flavors have melded, 1-2 minutes. Turn off heat; taste and season with salt and pepper if necessary.

instructions_json.title: Slice steak against the grain
instructions_json.body: Slice steak against the grain.Divide rice between shallow bowls and top with steak. Top steak with chili-lemon butter and remaining sesame seeds. Serve with pickled cucumber (draining first) and remaining lemon wedges on the side.Stir in remaining soy sauce and continue to cook, stirring constantly, until flavors have melded, 1-2 minutes. Turn off heat; taste and season with salt and pepper if necessary.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

title: Veggie Tempura Rice Bowls
subtitle: with Pickled Radishes & Shallot, Curry Mayo & Umami Ginger Sauce

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry produce. In a small pot, combine rice, 1¼ cups water (2¼ cups for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to a low simmer. Cook until rice is tender, 15-18 minutes. Keep covered off heat until ready to serve.

appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: While rice cooks, trim and slice radishes into ¼-inch-thick rounds. Halve, peel, and thinly slice shallot. Trim and slice zucchini crosswise on a diagonal into ½-inch-thick rounds. Halve, core, and slice bell pepper into ½-inch-thick strips. Slice sweet potato into ¼-inch-thick rounds.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: In a small bowl, combine curry paste and mayonnaise. In a separate small bowl, combine umami ginger sauce and half the vinegar.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: In a third small microwave-safe bowl, combine radishes, shallot, remaining vinegar, 1 TBSP water, ½ tsp sugar, and a pinch of salt (2 TBSP water and 1 tsp sugar for 4 servings); cover with plastic wrap and microwave for 40-60 seconds. Stir and set aside to pickle until ready to serve.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: In a large bowl, combine tempura batter mix, ⅔ cup cold water (1⅓ cups for 4 servings), and salt (we used ½ tsp; 1 tsp for 4) until smooth. TIP: If mixture seems too thick, add more water 1 TBSP at a time until it reaches a pancake-batter-like consistency. Pat zucchini very dry with paper towels; stir zucchini and bell pepper into batter until fully coated.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Heat a ⅓-inch layer of oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Once oil is hot enough that a drop of batter sizzles when added to the pan, working in batches, add coated zucchini and bell pepper in a single layer (let excess batter drip off into the bowl). Reserve remaining batter for next step. Cook coated zucchini and bell pepper, turning with tongs, until golden brown, 2-3 minutes per side. TIP: Lower heat if beginning to brown too quickly. Transfer zucchini and bell pepper to a paper-towel-lined plate; immediately season with salt. Remove pan from heat.

instructions_json.title: Step 7
instructions_json.body: Dip sweet potato into bowl with remaining batter until coated. Return pan with oil to medium-high heat. Once oil is hot enough that a drop of batter sizzles when added to the pan, add coated sweet potato in a single layer (let excess batter drip off into the bowl). Cook until crisped and lightly browned, 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer to paper-towel-lined plate and immediately season with salt. Divide tempura veggies, rice, and pickled veggies (draining first) between bowls. Serve with curry mayo and umami ginger sauce on the side for dipping.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a small pot, combine rice, 1¼ cups water (2¼ cups for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. Cook until tender, 15-18 minutes. Keep covered off heat until ready to serve.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: In a small microwave-safe bowl, combine ginger, scallion greens, 2 TBSP oil (4 TBSP for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Cover bowl with plastic wrap. Microwave until fragrant, 30 seconds. Stir and set aside.

instructions_json.title: Step 5

title: Banh Mi Bavette Steak & Lettuce Wraps
subtitle: with Pickled Veggies, Cilantro & Sriracha Aioli

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry produce. Halve, peel, and thinly slice shallot. Quarter lime. Trim and discard root end from lettuce; separate leaves. Roughly chop cilantro.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a medium microwave-safe bowl, combine carrots, shallot, vinegar, ¼ cup water, 1 tsp sugar, and a pinch of salt (½ cup water and 2 tsp sugar for 4 servings). Microwave until sugar has dissolved, 40-60 seconds. Set aside to pickle, stirring occasionally, until ready to serve. TIP: Taste and add another pinch of sugar if you like a sweeter pickle!

instructions_json.title: Step 3

instructions_json.title: Step 4

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Divide lettuce leaves between plates; fill with chicken and pickled veggies (draining first). Drizzle with sauce. Garnish with cilantro and serve with remaining lime wedges on the side.

instructions_json.body: Preheat air fryer to 400 degrees. Wash and dry produce. Dice sweet potatoes into ½-inch pieces. Quarter lemon. Open and drain tofu; press out excess water with paper towels. Halve crosswise, then stand tofu upright and halve vertically. Lay flat and cut into ½-inch cubes.

instructions_json.body: In a large bowl, toss sweet potatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Transfer sweet potatoes to air fryer basket; air-fry until slightly browned and tender, 7-10 minutes. (Keep empty bowl handy for Step 4!)

title: Buffalo Chicken & Cauliflower Tacos
subtitle: with Tangy-Sweet Slaw

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry produce. Trim and thinly slice scallions, separating whites from greens. Cut cauliflower florets into 1-inch pieces.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a medium bowl, combine coleslaw mix, mayonnaise, 1½ tsp vinegar (3 tsp for 4 servings), ¼ tsp sugar (½ tsp for 4), and a pinch of salt and pepper. (Save remaining vinegar for another use.)

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: In a second medium microwave-safe bowl, combine scallion whites, Frank’s hot sauce, hot sauce, 1 TBSP water (2 TBSP for 4 servings), a pinch of sugar, and a pinch of salt. Microwave on high for 1 minute, then immediately stir in 3 TBSP butter (6 TBSP for 4) until melted.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: In a third medium bowl (use a large bowl for 4 servings), whisk together tempura mix, Frank’s Seasoning Blend, ¼ cup water (½ cup for 4), and a pinch of salt and pepper. TIP: If mixture is too thick, add more water 1 tsp at a time until it reaches a pancake-batter-like consistency.Stir in cauliflower until fully coated.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Heat a ⅓-inch layer of oil in a large, preferably heavy-bottomed, pan over medium-high heat. Once oil is hot enough that a drop of batter sizzles when added to the pan, using a slotted spoon, add coated cauliflower. TIP: Don’t overcrowd the pan! You will need to work in batches. Cook until cauliflower is golden brown and crisp, 2-3 minutes per side. Using a slotted spoon, transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Wrap tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until warm and pliable, 30 seconds.Divide tortillas between plates; fill with slaw and cauliflower. Drizzle with sauce and sprinkle with scallion greens. Serve.

title: Cheesy Buffalo Pepperoni Strombolis
subtitle: with Buttermilk Ranch, Blue Cheese & Mixed Greens

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to middle position (middle and top positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 425 degrees. Wash and dry produce. Quarter lemon. Lightly coat a baking sheet (two baking sheets for 4) with a drizzle of olive oil. Remove pizza dough from packaging and roll dough balls on baking sheet to coat all over (for 4, divide dough between two sheets). Arrange dough balls on sheet at least 3 inches apart and cover with a clean kitchen towel; let rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Once dough has rested 20 minutes, gently press and stretch each dough ball into a 6-by-8-inch rectangle. (The dough is stretchy and the shapes won’t be perfect—that’s OK!) Repeat 2-3 times until dough forms a log with the filling enclosed. Arrange stromboli, seam side down, on baking sheet; pinch ends to close and tuck underneath. Repeat with remaining dough rectangle.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: With a sharp knife, gently cut three small, shallow diagonal slits along the top of each stromboli. Bake on middle rack until golden brown and crisp, 18-22 minutes. (For 4 servings, bake on middle and top racks, switching rack positions halfway through.)

instructions_json.body: Heat a large dry pan over medium-high heat. Add bacon; cook, turning occasionally and adjusting heat if browning too quickly, until crispy, 6-10 minutes. Turn off heat and transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Reserve pan.

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce

instructions_json.body: In a medium bowl, combine flour, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. In a separate medium bowl, stir to combine sour cream and 1½ TBSP water. instructions_json.title: Step 3

title: Creamy Butternut Squash Agnolotti with Chicken
subtitle: plus Zucchini, Thyme & Crispy Panko

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Wash and dry produce. Trim and dice zucchini into ¼-inch pieces. Halve, peel, and mince shallot. Melt 1 TBSP butter (2 TBSP for 4 servings) in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add panko; cook, stirring, until golden brown, 3-5 minutes. Turn off heat; transfer panko to a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Wipe out pan.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Heat pan used for panko over medium-high heat. Add bacon*; cook, turning occasionally and adjusting heat if browning too quickly, until crispy, 6-10 minutes. Turn off heat; transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Carefully discard all but a thin layer of bacon fat from pan (you’ll use it in Step 4). Once bacon is cool enough to handle, roughly chop.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Once water is boiling, add agnolotti to pot; reduce to a low simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente and floating to the top, 3-5 minutes. Reserve 1 cup pasta cooking water, then drain.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: While pasta cooks, heat pan with reserved bacon fat over medium-high heat. (TIP: If pan seems dry, add a drizzle of oil.) Add zucchini, shallot, and half the thyme (all for 4 servings); cook, stirring occasionally, until zucchini is lightly browned and shallot is softened, 2-3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: To pan with veggies, stir in cream cheese, garlic powder, stock concentrate, ½ cup reserved pasta cooking water, and 1 TBSP butter (¾ cup reserved pasta cooking water and 2 TBSP butter for 4 servings). Bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally. Once sauce is simmering, add drained agnolotti and bacon. Cook, stirring, until everything is coated in sauce, 1-2 minutes. TIP: If needed, stir in more reserved pasta cooking water a splash at a time.

instructions_json.title: Divide pasta between shallow bowls
instructions_json.body: Divide pasta between shallow bowls. Sprinkle with toasted panko and serve.

instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to top position (top and middle positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 475 degrees. Wash and dry produce. Sprinkle 3 tbsp flour over a clean work surface. Remove pizza dough from packaging and place on floured surface. Shape each piece of dough into a ball. (TIP: Spray your hands with nonstick cooking spray or dust with flour to prevent sticking.) Evenly sprinkle dough balls with 2 tbsp flour. Cover with a clean kitchen towel and let rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: While dough rests, halve, peel, and thinly slice onion. Trim and thinly slice mushrooms (skip if your mushrooms are pre-sliced!). Strip thyme leaves from stems; discard stems and roughly chop half the leaves (reserve remaining thyme for garnish).

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat a large drizzle of oil in a large, preferably nonstick, pan over medium-high heat. Add Italian Chicken Sausage Mix; cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes. Add onion; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, 3-4 minutes. Add mushrooms and chopped thyme; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are softened, 5 minutes. (TIP: If pan looks dry, add another drizzle of oil.) Add garlic powder, 1 tsp sugar (2 tsp for 4 servings), and ¼ cup water. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is jammy and caramelized and mushrooms are browned and tender, 2-3 minutes more. Season with salt and pepper. (For 4, you may need to work in batches.)

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Once dough has rested 20 minutes, line a baking sheet (two baking sheets for 4 servings) with parchment paper. Carefully press and stretch each dough ball into a rough oval shape and place on one side of prepared sheet (you’ll have two dough ovals per sheet). TIP: If needed, use a rolling pin to help roll out dough.Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest 15 minutes. (This will make stretching the dough into a larger shape even easier!)

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Once dough has rested 15 minutes, use floured hands to press and stretch dough on baking sheet into larger oval shapes, about 10 inches long and 5-6 inches wide. Evenly spread dough with roasted onion and garlic spread, leaving a 1-inch border. Sprinkle with mozzarella. Top with sausage, caramelized onion, and mushroom mixture and feta. Drizzle or brush edges of dough with olive oil.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Bake flatbreads on top rack until crusts are golden brown and crisp, 14-18 minutes. (For 4 servings, bake on top and middle racks, swapping rack positions halfway through.)

instructions_json.title: Step 7
instructions_json.body: Sprinkle reserved thyme leaves over flatbreads. Slice as desired and serve.

title: Brazilian-Style Organic Chicken Moqueca & Rice
subtitle: with Green Pepper, Onion & Cilantro

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: In a small pot, combine rice, ¾ cup water (1½ cups for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. Cook until rice is tender, 15-18 minutes.Keep covered off heat until ready to serve.

appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

instructions_json.title: While rice cooks, wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: While rice cooks, wash and dry produce.Quarter lime. Halve, peel, and dice onion into ½-inch pieces. Core, deseed, and dice green pepper into ½-inch pieces. Finely chop cilantro. Peel and mince three garlic cloves (six cloves for 4 servings).Rinse shrimp* under cold water; pat very dry with paper towels, then place in a medium bowl. Squeeze juice from half the lime over shrimp and toss to coat. Set aside to marinate until ready to use.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat a large drizzle of olive oil in a medium pot (large pot for 4 servings) over medium-high heat. Add onion, green pepper, and half the cilantro; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies begin to soften, 2-3 minutes.Add Southwest Spice Blend and minced garlic. Cook, stirring, until fragrant, 30 seconds more.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Add tomato paste to pot with veggies and cook, stirring, until beginning to darken slightly, 15-30 seconds.Stir in ¾ cup water (1½ cups for 4 servings), coconut milk, and stock concentrates. Bring to a simmer. TIP: Coconut milk may have some lumps—that’s OK! Whisk until no lumps remain.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Once soup is simmering, add marinated shrimp to pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until shrimp are opaque and cooked through, 4-6 minutes.Remove from heat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

instructions_json.title: Fluff rice with a fork
instructions_json.body: Fluff rice with a fork.Divide shrimp moqueca between bowls. Garnish with remaining cilantro. Place a mound of rice in the center of each bowl. Serve with remaining lime wedges on the side.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.
appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

title: Tandoori Rib-Eye & Cucumber Cilantro Raita
subtitle: Enjoy an abundant 3-course meal with a main, sides, and appetizers

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to middle position (middle and top positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 350 degrees.In a small pot, combine rice, ¾ cup water (1½ cups for 4), and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. Cook until rice is tender, 15-18 minutes.Keep covered off heat until ready to serve.

appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

instructions_json.title: While rice cooks, wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: While rice cooks, wash and dry produce.Dice cucumber into ¼-inch pieces. Finely chop cilantro. Zest and quarter lime.In a small bowl, combine cucumber, ½ tsp sugar (1 tsp for 4 servings), and salt. Set aside to marinate. (You’ll finish the raita in Step 6.)

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: In a large bowl, combine curry powder, half the yogurt, half the garlic-ginger scallion paste, half the cilantro, half the garam masala, and juice from half the lime.Pat pork* dry with paper towels and season all over with salt and pepper. Place in bowl with marinade, turning to fully coat. Set aside to marinate until ready to cook.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: While pork marinates, remove samosas from packaging. Place on a baking sheet about ½ inch apart and bake on middle rack until cooked through, 10-12 minutes. (For 4 servings, divide samosas between two sheets; bake on middle and top racks, swapping rack positions halfway through). Let stand a few minutes before serving.AIR FRYER ALTERNATIVE: Preheat air fryer to 350 degrees. Remove samosas from packaging. Place on an air fryer–safe pan about ½ inch apart. Air-fry until cooked through, 6-7 minutes. Let stand a few minutes before serving.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Cook protein in the Air Fryer at 390°F for 9-12 minutes until cooked through and caramelized.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan (or grill pan) over medium-high heat.Remove pork from marinade, allowing excess to drip off (discard remaining marinade). Add pork to pan; cook, undisturbed, until charred and cooked through, 4-6 minutes per side. TIP: Lower heat if pork begins to char too quickly. Turn off heat; transfer to a cutting board to rest for 5 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Fluff rice with a fork; stir in remaining garlic-ginger scallion paste.Wrap naan in damp paper towels and microwave until warm and pliable, 30 seconds.Drain excess liquid from marinated cucumber, then stir in remaining yogurt, remaining garam masala, remaining cilantro, lime zest, and juice from remaining lime.Thinly slice pork.Divide rice and pork between plates. Top pork with cucumber raita and mango chutney. Serve with samosas and naan family style on the side.

appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

title: Cheesy-Chili Verde Tacodillas & Bavette Steak
subtitle: with Lime Crema

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry produce.Zest and quarter lime. Trim and thinly slice scallions, separating whites from greens.Remove husks from tomatillos and rinse under warm water, gently scrubbing with your fingers (it’s OK if they feel sticky—that’s normal!). Pat dry with paper towels; cut into ¼-inch pieces.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a small bowl, stir together sour cream, lime zest, and juice from one lime wedge (two wedges for 4 servings). Add water 1 tsp at a time until mixture reaches a drizzling consistency. Season with salt and pepper.Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add scallion whites and tomatillos; cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften, 1-2 minutes.Taste and season with additional salt or pepper, if desired. Transfer mixture to a medium bowl; wash and thoroughly dry pan.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: To pan with tomatillos, stir in ⅓ cup water (½ cup for 4 servings) and stock concentrate. Bring to a simmer; add pork*, Fajita Spice Blend, ¼ tsp sugar (½ tsp for 4), and a big pinch of salt. Cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until sauce has thickened and pork is cooked through, 3-5 minutes more.Turn off heat. Taste and season with salt or pepper if desired. Transfer filling to a medium bowl; wash and thoroughly dry pan.

instructions_json.title: Place tortillas on a clean work surface
instructions_json.body: Place tortillas on a clean work surface.In a small bowl, combine mozzarella and Monterey Jack.Evenly sprinkle half the cheese blend over bottom half of each tortilla; top with pork filling and remaining cheese blend. Fold tortillas in half to create tacodillas.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Heat a large drizzle of oil in pan used for pork over medium heat. Add tacodillas and cook until tortillas are golden brown, 1-2 minutes per side. (For 4 servings, you may need to work in batches, adding a drizzle of oil between batches.)

instructions_json.title: Divide tacodillas between plates
instructions_json.body: Divide tacodillas between plates. Drizzle with lime crema and sprinkle with scallion greens. Serve with remaining lime wedges on the side.

title: Flautas Supreme with Organic Beef
subtitle: with Pico de Gallo & Smoky Red Pepper Crema

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to middle position and preheat oven to 425 degrees. Line a baking sheet with foil and brush with oil (or coat with nonstick spray). Wash and dry produce. Halve, peel, and thinly slice onion; mince a few slices until you have 1 TBSP (2 TBSP for 4 servings).

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced onion; cook for 3 minutes.Add beef* and Southwest Spice Blend; cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until beef is browned and onion is softened, 4-6 minutes. Stir in Tex-Mex paste and ⅓ cup water (½ cup for 4 servings). Simmer until thickened and beef is cooked through, 2-4 minutes more. Turn off heat.Stir in Tex-Mex paste and ⅓ cup water (½ cup for 4 servings). Simmer until mixture has thickened and beef is cooked through, 2-4 minutes more. Turn off heat.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Meanwhile, drizzle tortillas with 1 TBSP olive oil (2 TBSP for 4 servings); brush or rub to completely coat.Place tortillas on a clean work surface. Once beef filling is done, add a heaping ¼ cup filling to one side of each tortilla, then sprinkle each with 1 TBSP Mexican cheese blend. Roll up tortillas, starting with filled sides, to create flautas. Place, seam sides down, on prepared sheet. TIP: Make sure the flautas are snug on the sheet—this will prevent them from unrolling.Bake on middle rack until golden brown and crispy, 8-12 minutes.

instructions_json.title: While flautas bake, finely dice tomato
instructions_json.body: While flautas bake, finely dice tomato. In a small bowl, combine tomato and minced onion. Season with salt.Divide flautas between plates. Top with pico de gallo and red pepper crema. Serve.

title: Air Fryer Beef, Black Bean & Potato Flautas
subtitle: with Mexican Cheese, Black Beans & Fresh Tomato Salsa

instructions_json.title: Preheat air fryer to 375 degrees
instructions_json.body: Preheat air fryer to 375 degrees. Wash and dry produce.Drain and rinse beans. Roughly chop potatoes into ¼-inch pieces.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a medium bowl, combine beans, Tex-Mex paste, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Roughly mash beans with a potato masher or fork until about half are mashed.Stir in potatoes.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Wrap tortillas in damp paper towels and microwave until warm and pliable, 30 seconds.Place tortillas on a clean work surface. Drizzle with 1 TBSP oil (2 TBSP for 4 servings); brush or rub to completely coat on both sides.Add a heaping ¼ cup filling to one side of each tortilla. Top filling with Mexican cheese blend. instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Carefully place flautas, seam sides down, in air fryer. Air-fry until golden brown and crispy, 6-8 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Meanwhile, dice tomatoes into ¼-inch pieces. Quarter limes.In a small bowl (medium bowl for 4 servings), combine tomatoes, juice from half the limes, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Divide flautas between plates and top with sour cream and salsa (draining first). Serve with remaining lime wedges on the side. TIP: If you have any remaining filling, add a drizzle of olive oil and microwave until warm, 30-60 seconds. Serve flautas over filling.

instructions_json.title: Step 3

Add remaining beans and cook, stirring, until slightly softened, 2-3 minutes.Add ¼ cup reserved bean liquid (½ cup for 4 servings). title: Southwest Corn & Zucchini Flautas
subtitle: with Enchilada Sauce & Queso Blanco

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to top position and preheat oven to 425 degrees. Line a baking sheet with foil and brush with oil. Wash and dry produce. Trim zucchini and grate on the largest holes of a box grater. Place in the center of a clean kitchen towel. Gather into a tight bundle and squeeze over the sink to remove as much liquid as possible. Drain corn, then pat dry with paper towels. Trim and thinly slice scallions, separating whites from greens.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add zucchini and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and softened, 3-4 minutes. Add corn and scallion whites; cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and lightly charred in spots, 2-4 minutes. TIP: Cover pan if corn starts to pop. Add Southwest Spice Blend and half the enchilada sauce; cook, stirring often, until thickened, 1-2 minutes. Turn off heat; stir in Monterey Jack until melted. Taste and season with salt and pepper if desired.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Meanwhile, drizzle tortillas with 1 TBSP olive oil (2 TBSP for 4 servings); brush or rub to completely coat on both sides. Place tortillas on a clean work surface. Once corn and zucchini filling is done, add a heaping ¼ cup filling to one side of each tortilla. Roll up tortillas, starting with filled sides, to create flautas. Place flautas, seam sides down, on prepared sheet. TIP: Arrange your flautas snug on the sheet to keep them from unrolling.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Bake flautas on top rack until golden brown and crispy, 8-12 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Place remaining enchilada sauce in a small microwave-safe bowl. Microwave until warmed through, 45-60 seconds. In a second small microwave-safe bowl, combine queso blanco with 1 TBSP water (2 TBSP for 4 servings); microwave until warmed through, 25 seconds.

instructions_json.title: Divide flautas between plates
instructions_json.body: Divide flautas between plates. Drizzle with queso blanco and as much remaining enchilada sauce as you like. Sprinkle with scallion greens and serve.

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: • Adjust rack to middle position and preheat oven to 425 degrees. Wash and dry produce. • Trim, peel, and cut carrots into sticks (like fries; ours were 3 inches long and 1⁄3 inch thick). Cut waffles into 1-inch-wide strips.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: • Open package of chicken* and drain off any excess liquid. Season all over with salt and pepper. • Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken in a single layer; cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes. TIP: Cut any larger pieces of cooked chicken into bite-size pieces. • Transfer chicken to a medium bowl; add Mexican cheese blend and as much guacamole as you like. Stir to combine.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: • Wrap tortillas in damp paper towels; microwave until warm and pliable, 30 seconds. • Lay tortillas on a clean work surface. Evenly divide chicken mixture between one half of each tortilla. Lightly season with salt and pepper if desired. Roll up tortillas, starting with filled sides, to create flautas. • Place flautas, seam sides down, on a lightly oiled baking sheet. Brush tops with a drizzle of oil. Bake on middle rack until golden brown and warmed through, 6-8 minutes.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Cook protein in the Air Fryer at 390°F for 9-12 minutes until cooked through and caramelized.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: • To serve: Halve flautas on a diagonal; divide between plates. Serve with carrot sticks and waffle sticks on the side. • To stash: Let flautas cool completely before halving. Refrigerate flautas, carrot sticks, and waffle sticks in separate containers and pack as desired!

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: • Adjust rack to middle position (top and middle positions for 6 servings) and preheat oven to 375 degrees. • Remove buttermilk biscuits from package. Using a rolling pin, roll out each biscuit to form a 3-inch round. TIP: Lightly dust work surface with flour to prevent sticking. • Place 1 tsp marinara sauce in center of each circle; divide half the mozzarella between circles. Gently fold edges over filling and pinch tightly to close. Gently roll each pizza popper into a ball.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: • Line a second baking sheet with foil and coat with nonstick cooking spray. Place pizza poppers, sealed sides down, 2 inches apart on prepared baking sheet (divide between two sheets for 6 servings). Brush tops with oil and sprinkle with remaining mozzarella. • Bake on middle rack (top and middle racks for 6) until golden brown, 15-18 minutes. Let cool completely; divide between plates and serve with remaining marinara sauce. Chicken is fully cooked when internal temperature reaches 165°.

title: Chicken & Green Pepper Flautas
subtitle: with Black Beans, Guacamole, Pico de Gallo & Sour Cream

instructions_json.title: • Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: • Wash and dry produce. • Finely dice tomato. Trim and thinly slice scallions. Halve lime. Halve, peel, and thinly slice onion. Core, deseed, and cut green pepper into ½-inch pieces. Drain beans over a small bowl, reserving liquid. • In a separate small bowl, combine tomato, scallions, a big squeeze of lime juice, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: • Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and green pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until just softened, 5-6 minutes. • Add Southwest Spice Blend and half the beans (you’ll use the rest in the next step). Cook, stirring, until fragrant and warmed through, 2-3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Pat chicken dry with paper towels. Add chicken or beef to pan along with onion and green pepper; cook, stirring frequently, until meat is cooked through and veggies are softened, 4-6 minutes. Cook through the rest of the step as instructed.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: • Meanwhile, heat a drizzle of oil in a small pot over medium-high heat. Add remaining beans and cook, stirring, until slightly softened, 2-3 minutes. • Add ¼ cup reserved bean liquid (½ cup for 4 servings). Simmer until warmed through, 1-2 minutes. • Reduce heat to low and stir in 1 TBSP butter until melted. • Remove pot from heat; mash beans until mostly smooth. Season with plenty of salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: • Spread tortillas with mashed beans
instructions_json.body: • Spread tortillas with mashed beans. Place a small amount of filling on one half of each tortilla, then sprinkle with pepper jack. • Roll up tortillas, starting with filled sides, to create flautas. Place, seam sides down, on a plate or work surface. • Wash out pan.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: • Heat a large drizzle of oil in same pan over medium-high heat. Add flautas, seam sides down. Cook, turning carefully so they stay intact, until golden brown and crispy, 1-2 minutes per side. TIP: Work in batches if necessary and watch carefully to avoid burning.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: • Divide flautas between plates and top with guacamole, pico de gallo, and sour cream. (Alternatively, serve with toppings on the side for dipping.) Cut remaining lime half into wedges and serve on the side. Chicken is fully cooked when internal temperature reaches 165°.

title: Smashed Black Bean Tostadas with Beef
subtitle: with Green Pepper, Pico de Gallo & Lime Crema

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to top position (top and middle positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 450 degrees. Wash and dry produce. Halve, peel, and thinly slice onion; mince a few slices until you have 2 tbsp (4 tbsp for 4 servings). Dice tomatoes. Roughly chop cilantro. Quarter lime. Halve, core, and thinly slice green pepper into strips. Drain and rinse beans. In a small bowl, combine minced onion, tomatoes, half the cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice. Season with salt and pepper. In a separate small bowl, combine sour cream with a squeeze of lime juice. Add water 1 tsp at a time until mixture reaches a drizzling consistency. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes. Add green pepper, sliced onion, and half the Southwest Spice Blend (you’ll use the rest in the next step). Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly charred and softened, 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Turn off heat; transfer to a plate.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat pan used for veggies over medium-high heat. Add beans, Tex-Mex paste, remaining Southwest Spice Blend, and ¼ cup water (⅓ cup for 4 servings). Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid has mostly evaporated, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat; gently mash beans with a potato masher or the back of a spoon. Stir in 1 tbsp butter (2 tbsp for 4 servings) until melted. (TIP: If mixture is too thick, stir in a splash of water.) Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Drizzle tortillas with 1 tbsp olive oil (2 tbsp for 4 servings); brush or rub to coat all over. Arrange on a baking sheet in a single layer (divide between 2 sheets for 4 servings). Gently prick each tortilla in a few places with a fork. Bake on top rack, flipping halfway through, until lightly golden, 4-5 minutes per side. (For 4, bake on top and middle racks, flipping tortillas and swapping rack positions halfway through.) TIP: Watch carefully to avoid burning.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Once tortillas are toasted, remove sheet from oven. Carefully spread each tortilla with smashed beans, then top with beef and veggies and Mexican cheese blend. Return to top rack (top and middle racks for 4 servings) and bake until cheese melts, 2-3 minutes.

title: Tostadas with Mexican-Style Tuna Salad

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry produce. Mince jalapeño, removing ribs and seeds for less heat. Drain corn and pat dry with paper towels. Dice tomato into ¼-inch pieces. Halve, peel, and mince shallot. Finely chop cilantro. Zest and quarter lime.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a small microwave-safe bowl, combine jalapeño, vinegar, ½ tsp sugar (1 tsp for 4 servings), salt, and pepper. Cover with plastic wrap and microwave until jalapeño is softened, 30 seconds. Keep covered, stirring occasionally, until ready to use in Step 5.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over high heat. Add corn; season with a pinch of sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and lightly charred in spots, 4-6 minutes. (Cover pan with a lid if corn starts to pop!) Turn off heat; transfer corn to a large bowl. Wipe out pan.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Heat a large drizzle of oil in same pan over medium-high heat. Working in batches, add tortillas and cook until crisped and golden, 1-3 minutes per side. TIP: Add more oil in between batches if pan looks dry; lower heat if browning too quickly. Transfer tortillas to a paper-towel-lined plate until ready to assemble tostadas in Step 6.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: To bowl with charred corn, add tuna, tomato, shallot, half the cilantro, half the mayonnaise, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, pepper, and as much chili powder as you like. Stir until thoroughly combined. Drain jalapeño, reserving pickling liquid. In a second small bowl, stir together sour cream, lime zest, drained jalapeño, remaining mayonnaise, and splashes of pickling liquid until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Divide tortillas between plates and top with tuna salad. Drizzle with jalapeño crema and sprinkle with remaining cilantro. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

Wash and dry produce.Halve, peel, and thinly slice half the onion; finely chop remaining half until you have 2 TBSP (for 4 servings, thinly slice whole onion; finely chop a few slices until you have 3 TBSP). Dice tomato. Roughly chop cilantro. Quarter lime. Halve, core, and thinly slice green pepper into strips.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a small bowl, combine chopped onion, tomato, cilantro, juice from half the lime, and a pinch of salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add beef*; season with Southwest Spice Blend, salt, and pepper. Cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes. Turn off heat; transfer to a plate. Wipe out pan.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in pan used for beef over medium-high heat. Add sliced onion and green pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and tender, 5-7 minutes. Season with chili powder, salt, and pepper. Stir in cooked beef, stock concentrate, and ¼ cup water. Cook until mixture is thickened and saucy, 1-2 minutes. (TIP: If mixture seems dry, add another splash of water.)

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Meanwhile, drizzle tortillas with 1 TBSP oil (2 TBSP for 4 servings); brush or rub to coat all over. Arrange on a baking sheet in a single layer (for 4, divide between 2 baking sheets). Gently prick each tortilla in a few places with a fork.Toast on top rack, carefully flipping tortillas halfway through, until lightly golden, 4-5 minutes per side. (For 4, toast on top and middle racks, flipping tortillas and swapping rack positions halfway through toasting.) TIP: Watch carefully to avoid burning.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Divide tortillas between plates; evenly sprinkle with Mexican cheese blend. Top with beef and veggies, pico de gallo, and smoky red pepper crema. Drizzle with hot sauce to taste. Serve with remaining lime wedges on the side.

title: Smashed Black Bean & Turkey Tostadas
subtitle: with Green Pepper, Pico de Gallo & Lime Crema

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to top position (top and middle positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 450 degrees. Wash and dry produce. Halve, peel, and thinly slice onion; mince a few slices until you have 2 TBSP (4 TBSP for 4 servings). Dice tomatoes. Roughly chop cilantro. Quarter lime. Halve, core, and thinly slice green pepper into strips. Drain and rinse beans. In a small bowl, combine minced onion, tomatoes, half the cilantro, and a squeeze of lime juice. Season with salt and pepper. In a separate small bowl, combine sour cream with a squeeze of lime juice. Add water 1 tsp at a time until mixture reaches a drizzling consistency. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add turkey and half the Southwest Spice Blend (you’ll use the rest in the next step). Cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until browned and cooked through, 4-6 minutes. Add green pepper and sliced onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly charred and softened, 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Turn off heat; transfer to a plate.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat pan used for veggies over medium-high heat. Add beans, Tex-Mex paste, remaining Southwest Spice Blend, and ¼ cup water (⅓ cup for 4 servings). Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid has mostly evaporated, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat; gently mash beans with a potato masher or the back of a spoon. Stir in 1 TBSP butter (2 TBSP for 4) until melted. (TIP: If mixture is too thick, stir in a splash of water.) Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Drizzle tortillas with 1 TBSP olive oil (2 TBSP for 4 servings); brush or rub to coat all over. Arrange on a baking sheet in a single layer (divide between 2 sheets for 4). Gently prick each tortilla in a few places with a fork.Bake on top rack, flipping halfway through, until lightly golden, 4-5 minutes per side. (For 4, bake on top and middle racks, flipping tortillas and swapping rack positions halfway through.) TIP: Watch carefully to avoid burning.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Once tortillas are toasted, remove sheet from oven. Carefully spread each tortilla with smashed beans, then top with turkey and veggies and Mexican cheese blend. Return to top rack (top and middle racks for 4 servings) and bake until cheese melts, 2-3 minutes.

appliance_override.air_fryer: Air Fryer Adaptation: Toss coated veggies/potatoes in the Air Fryer basket at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking halfway through until golden and crisp.

instructions_json.title: Divide tostadas between plates
instructions_json.body: Divide tostadas between plates. Top with pico de gallo, lime crema, and remaining cilantro. Serve with remaining lime wedges on the side.

subtitle: with Green Bell Pepper, Tomato Salsa & Hot Sauce Crema

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to top position (top and middle positions for 4 servings) and preheat oven to 450 degrees. Wash and dry produce.Dice tomato. Roughly chop cilantro. Halve and peel onion; thinly slice one half. Finely chop remaining onion until you have 2 TBSP. Quarter lime. Halve, core, and thinly slice bell pepper into strips.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: In a medium bowl, combine tomato, cilantro, chopped onion, juice from half the lime, and a pinch of salt and pepper.In a small bowl, combine sour cream with as much hot sauce as you like. Stir in water 1 tsp at a time until mixture reaches a drizzling consistency. Season with salt.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add beef*, Southwest Spice Blend, chili powder, and a few big pinches of salt. Cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until browned, 4-5 minutes (it’ll finish cooking in the next step).

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Once beef is browned, add bell pepper, sliced onion, and a pinch of salt to pan. Cook, stirring, until veggies are tender and beef is cooked through, 5-7 minutes.Add stock concentrate and ¼ cup water (½ cup water for 4 servings). Simmer until thickened, 1-2 minutes. Season with salt; remove pan from heat and set aside.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Drizzle tortillas with 1 TBSP olive oil (2 TBSP for 4 servings); brush or rub to coat all over. Arrange on a baking sheet in a single layer (divide between two sheets for 4). Gently prick each tortilla in a few places with a fork.Bake on top rack, flipping halfway through, until lightly golden, 4-5 minutes per side. (For 4, bake on top and middle racks; flip tortillas and swap rack positions halfway through baking.) TIP: Watch carefully—tortillas brown fast!

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Divide tortillas between plates; evenly sprinkle with Mexican cheese blend. Top with beef mixture, salsa, and crema. Serve with remaining lime wedges on the side.

title: Tex-Mex Zucchini & Chicken Casserole
subtitle: with Dark Meat Chicken, Couscous & Three Beans

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to top position and preheat oven to 425 degrees. Wash and dry produce.Trim and halve zucchini lengthwise; scoop out seedy cores with a spoon (set zucchini halves aside for use in next step). Roughly chop zucchini cores. Drain and rinse corn; thoroughly pat dry with paper towels. Halve, peel, and finely dice onion. Drain and rinse beans. Finely chop cilantro.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Rub zucchini halves all over with 2 tsp olive oil (4 tsp for 4 servings); season with salt and pepper. Arrange, cut sides down, on a baking sheet. Roast on top rack until browned and tender, 15-20 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Meanwhile, in a small pot, combine couscous, stock concentrate, 1 cup water (2 cups for 4 servings), and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, cover and reduce to a low simmer. Cook until couscous is tender, 6-8 minutes.Drain any excess water if necessary. Keep covered off heat until ready to use in Step 5.

appliance_override.rice_cooker: Rice Cooker Adaptation: Combine rinsed grains, water, and a pinch of salt in the Rice Cooker. Run the standard cycle, then fluff and fold in butter/seasonings before serving.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over high heat. Add corn; season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and lightly charred in spots, 4-6 minutes. (Cover pan with a lid if corn starts to pop!) Turn off heat; transfer to a small bowl. Wipe out pan. Heat a large drizzle of oil in same pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and chopped zucchini cores; season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is softened, 3-5 minutes. TIP: Add another drizzle of oil if pan seems dry!

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Stir cooked couscous, charred corn, beans, half the cilantro, and ⅔ cup enchilada sauce (1⅓ cups for 4 servings) into pan with onion mixture. Cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 2-3 minutes. (Add another splash of enchilada sauce or water if mixture seems dry.) Taste and season with salt and pepper.Place mayonnaise in a second small bowl. Add water 1 tsp at a time until mixture reaches a drizzling consistency. Taste and season with salt and pepper if desired.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Transfer couscous to a serving dish and arrange roasted zucchini on top, cut sides down. Drizzle everything with vegan mayo sauce and as much hot sauce as you like. Top with remaining cilantro and serve family style.

instructions_json.title: Step 3

instructions_json.title: Step 4

title: Creamy Chicken Pasta Casserole
subtitle: with Broccoli, Ranch Seasoning, and Three Cheeses

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Adjust broiler rack so that it is in position closest to flame and heat broiler to high. Once water is boiling, add cavatappi to pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until just al dente, about 8 minutes. Drain.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Meanwhile, pat chicken dry with paper towel. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 2 TBSP olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat (use an ovenproof pan if you have one). Add chicken and cook until browned and no longer pink in center, 5-6 minutes per side. Remove from pan and set aside.

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry all produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry all produce. Place broccoli and 1 TBSP water in a medium, microwave-safe bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and poke a few holes in wrap. Microwave on high until tender, about 3 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Melt 2 TBSP butter in pan used for chicken over medium-high heat. Add flour and ranch spice. Stir constantly until pasty and fragrant, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Slowly whisk in milk, scraping up any browned bits on bottom. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium. Let bubble until sauce thickens slightly, about 3 minutes. Remove pan from heat.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Add cream cheese, cheddar, and ½ cup mozzarella (1 pack) to pan and whisk until smooth (we’ll use the rest of the mozzarella later). Season with salt and pepper. Thinly slice chicken. Drain broccoli. Stir chicken, broccoli, and cavatappi into pan. Season with salt and pepper. (TIP: If your pan isn’t ovenproof, transfer mixture to a baking dish at this point.) Place 1 TBSP butter in a small, microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on high until it melts, about 45 seconds.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Add ¼ cup panko (we sent more) and remaining mozzarella to bowl with butter and stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper. Scatter over pasta in pan or dish. Place pan under broiler and broil until cheese melts and panko is golden brown, about 3 minutes. Divide pasta between plates and serve.

title: Shrimp Pasta With a Kick
subtitle: with Garlic Herb Butter and Zucchini

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry all produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry all produce. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Once boiling, add pasta and cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente, 10-12 minutes. Carefully scoop out and reserve ½ cup pasta cooking water, then drain.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Meanwhile, halve zucchini lengthwise, then slice into ¼-inch-thick half-moons. Thinly slice half the chili (if you like it spicy, feel free to use all). Rinse shrimp, then pat dry with a paper towel, removing as much moisture as you can.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Heat a large drizzle of olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add zucchini and chili and cook, tossing occasionally, until zucchini is lightly browned, about 2 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Push zucchini to one side of pan and add another large drizzle of olive oil to center. Add shrimp and cook, tossing occasionally, until pink and just cooked through, 3-4 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Add pasta, garlic herb butter, half the Parmesan, and ¼ cup pasta cooking water to pan. Season with plenty of salt and pepper. Toss until combined and coated in a loose sauce. TIP: Add remaining ¼ cup pasta cooking water, as needed, if mixture seems dry.

instructions_json.title: Divide pasta between bowls
instructions_json.body: Divide pasta between bowls. Sprinkle with remaining Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil. TIP: Garnish with additional chili (to taste) for extra heat.

title: Beefy Taco Casserole
subtitle: with Mixed Green Salad

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry all produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry all produce. Preheat oven to 425 degrees. Halve, peel, and finely chop onion. Mince or grate garlic. Thinly slice scallions.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over high heat. Add ground beef and break up into pieces with a spatula or wooden spoon. Cook until browned, 4-5 minutes. Stir in Mexican spice blend and season with salt and pepper. Remove from pan and set aside.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Add onions, garlic, and a drizzle of oil to same pan over medium heat. Cook until softened, 4-5 minutes. Stir in 2 tsp Southwest spice blend (we sent more) and half the scallions. Cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in diced tomatoes and ground beef. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Place a layer of filling in a small baking dish (ours is 11 x 7). Top with 2 tortillas, tearing to fit. (TIP: It's OK if tortillas don't cover filling completely.) Add a layer of Monterey Jack cheese. Repeat with three more layers, finishing with a layer of filling and cheese.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Bake casserole until melted and bubbling, 5-7 minutes. (TIP: For a golden and crispy top, heat broiler to high and broil casserole a further 2-3 minutes.) Meanwhile, halve lime. Halve grape tomatoes. Toss mixed greens and grape tomatoes in a large bowl with a squeeze of lime and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: Sprinkle casserole with remaining scallions. (TIP: If you have time, let rest a few minutes for cleaner slices.) Cut casserole into slices and serve with salad and a dollop of sour cream on the side.

title: Orzo and Chorizo Casserole
subtitle: with Burst Tomatoes, Mozzarella, and Spinach

instructions_json.title: Wash and dry all produce
instructions_json.body: Wash and dry all produce. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees. Halve, peel, and dice the onion. Mince or grate the garlic. Halve the tomatoes. Strip the thyme off the sprigs and roughly chop the leaves. Remove the chorizo from its casing. Bring a large pot of salted water (at least 6 cups) to a boil.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Cook the onion and garlic: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic to the pan and cook, tossing for 4-5 minutes, until softened. Season with salt and pepper.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Roast the tomatoes: Toss the tomatoes on a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Place in the oven for about 10 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Add the thyme, chorizo, and 2 Tablespoons tomato paste to the pan with the onions. Cook, breaking up the chorizo into pieces, tossing for 4-5 minutes, until the chorizo browns.

instructions_json.title: Add the orzo to the pan and toss to coat
instructions_json.body: Add the orzo to the pan and toss to coat. Add 5 cups of the salted water and the stock concentrates to the pan. Reduce to a low simmer and cook for 9-11 minutes, until the orzo is almost al dente. Season with salt and pepper. TIP: If the water absorbs before the orzo is tender, add another splash of water.

instructions_json.title: Step 6
instructions_json.body: When the orzo is tender, stir in the mozzarella cheese, burst tomatoes, and parmesan cheese. Place the spinach on top and cover for 2-3 minutes to steam. Stir to combine and season generously with salt and pepper, to taste. Serve straight out of the pan and enjoy!

title: Roasted Tomato & Garlic Bisque
subtitle: with Grilled Cheese Croutons

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Adjust rack to top position and preheat oven to 450 degrees. Wash and dry produce. Peel garlic and place whole cloves in the center of a small piece of foil; drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Cinch into a packet. Quarter Roma tomatoes.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: On a foil-lined baking sheet, toss grape tomatoes and quartered Roma tomatoes with a large drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread out in an even layer. Add garlic packet to sheet. Roast on top rack until tomatoes are lightly browned and garlic is tender, 20-25 minutes. Meanwhile, halve, peel, and dice onion into ½-inch pieces.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Melt 2 TBSP butter (4 TBSP for 4 servings) in a medium pot (large pot for 4) over medium heat. Add onion and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6-8 minutes. Stir in basil paste, stock concentrates, and roasted onion and garlic spread. Add ½ cup water (1 cup for 4), marinara, and cream sauce base; stir to combine.

instructions_json.title: Step 4
instructions_json.body: Reduce heat under pot to medium low; cover and cook, stirring occasionally, while tomatoes and garlic roast. Once tomatoes and garlic are done, carefully remove garlic packet from baking sheet. Transfer roasted tomatoes to pot with soup. Carefully remove roasted garlic from foil and stir into pot. Remove from heat.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Using an immersion blender, blend soup directly in pot until smooth, 2-4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste. TIP: Don’t have an immersion blender? Carefully transfer soup to a blender or food processor. Pulse until smooth, then transfer back to pot. Cover soup with lid and keep warm over low heat until ready to serve.

instructions_json.title: Lay bread out on a clean work surface
instructions_json.body: Lay bread out on a clean work surface. Evenly layer half the bread slices with cheddar; top with remaining bread slices to form sandwiches. Heat a large drizzle of olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add sandwiches and cook, gently pressing with a spatula, until bread is golden and cheese melts, 2-4 minutes per side, adding another drizzle of olive oil if needed when flipping. TIP: Work in batches if necessary; lower heat if browning too quickly.

instructions_json.title: Step 7
instructions_json.body: Cut grilled cheese sandwiches into 1-inch cubes. Divide roasted tomato and garlic bisque between bowls. Top with grilled cheese croutons. Serve. TIP: If you like your soup with a spicy kick, garnish with chili flakes or your favorite hot sauce!

title: Herb-Grilled Sirloin Steak & Old Bay Shrimp
subtitle: with Caesar Salad & Garlic Bread

instructions_json.title: Step 1
instructions_json.body: Preheat a well-oiled grill to medium-high heat. (TIP: If using a grill pan, you’ll heat it in step 4.) Place garlic herb butter in a small bowl; bring to room temperature. Wash and dry produce. Finely chop parsley leaves and stems. Trim and discard root end from lettuce; chop leaves into bite-size pieces. Halve tomatoes lengthwise. Halve baguette lengthwise. Zest and quarter lemon.

instructions_json.title: Step 2
instructions_json.body: Place 3 TBSP plain butter (6 TBSP for 4 servings) in a second small, microwave-safe bowl. Microwave until just softened, 10-15 seconds.Stir in 1 TBSP parsley (2 TBSP for 4) and ¾ tsp Old Bay Seasoning (1½ tsp for 4) until combined. Set aside for serving.

instructions_json.title: Step 3
instructions_json.body: Toss lettuce, tomatoes, and Parmesan together in a large bowl. (You’ll add the dressing in step 6.) Set aside.

instructions_json.title: Pat steak* dry with paper towels
instructions_json.body: Pat steak* dry with paper towels. Season all over with half the Ranch Spice (all for 4 servings), salt, and pepper.Rinse shrimp* under cold water, then pat dry with paper towels. Place in the center of a large piece of foil; add a large drizzle of oil and remaining Old Bay Seasoning. Cinch into a packet.Add steak and shrimp packet to grill. (TIP: For a grill pan, oil and heat over medium-high heat. Work in batches.) Grill steak to desired doneness, 4-8 minutes per side. Grill shrimp until cooked through, 8-10 minutes (grills can vary). Remove from heat. Transfer steak to a cutting board to rest for at least 5 minutes.PAN ALTERNATIVE: Cook seasoned steak in a large oiled pan over medium-high heat, 5-7 minutes per side. Transfer to a cutting board to rest for 5 minutes. Wipe out pan. Season shrimp with remaining Old Bay Seasoning (skip the foil packet). Cook in same oiled pan over medium-high heat, stirring, 3-4 minutes.

instructions_json.title: Step 5
instructions_json.body: Once steak and shrimp are cooked, reduce heat on grill or grill pan to medium. Spread cut sides of baguette with half the softened garlic herb butter.Add bread to grill, cut sides down. Grill until toasted, 1-3 minutes. TIP: Watch carefully to avoid burning! Once bread has cooled, carefully spread cut sides with remaining softened garlic herb butter. Halve on a diagonal.TOASTER ALTERNATIVE: Toast baguette until golden. Spread cut sides with softened garlic herb butter.

instructions_json.title: Carefully open shrimp foil packet
instructions_json.body: Carefully open shrimp foil packet. Add lemon zest, remaining parsley, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Toss to combine.Add Caesar dressing and a squeeze of lemon juice to bowl with salad. Toss to combine. Season with salt and pepper.Slice steak against the grain.Divide salad, steak, shrimp, and garlic bread between plates. Top steak with parsley butter and serve.PAN ALTERNATIVE: Toss shrimp in pan.
